title: 1000 Layer Networks for Self-Supervised RL: Scaling Depth Can Enable New G

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix A.2 table after Figure 13 (Scaled CRL (Ours) rows) vs Table 1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Appendix table reports Scaled CRL values for Humanoid as Depth 4 = 19.5, Depth 64 = 756; for Ant Big Maze as Depth 4 = 60.7, Depth 64 = 441; for Arm Push Easy as Depth 64 = 762. Table 1 reports Humanoid D4 = 12.6 ± 1.3, D64 = 530 ± 19; Ant Big Maze D64 = 420 ± 25; Arm Push Easy D64 = 620 ± 30. The Humanoid and Arm Push numbers are substantially inconsistent without any explanation.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 3 vs Table 4 (Humanoid U-Maze wall-clock times)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 3 lists Humanoid U-Maze wall-clock time as D4 = 8.72 h, D8 = 11.29 h, D16 = 16.36 h, D32 = 26.48 h, D64 = 46.74 h. Table 4, also for Humanoid U-Maze, lists D4 = 3.23 h, D8 = 4.19 h, D16 = 6.07 h, D32 = 9.83 h, D64 = 17.33 h. The two tables cannot both be correct for the same environment/depth without a stated difference in protocol.

The paper states 'the parameter count scales linearly with width but quadratically with depth.' For dense residual MLPs, params ≈ depth × width² (plus smaller input/output terms), so parameter count scales linearly with depth and quadratically with width. Appendix B.6 later correctly says FLOPs and memory 'scale quadratically with width but only linearly with depth,' directly contradicting the main-text sentence.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.4, 'Deep Networks Unlock Batch Size Scaling' / Figure 7
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The subsection title and opening claim say deeper networks 'can effectively leverage batch size scaling to achieve further improvements.' The same section then states: 'Figure 7 shows only marginal or inconsistent improvements from increasing batch size, even for larger depth models. While larger networks can handle larger batches without degradation, the overall benefit of batch size scaling remains uncertain.' These statements directly contradict each other.

There are two different figures numbered 12: Section 4.4 has 'Figure 12: Testing the limits of scale,' while Appendix A.1 has 'Figure 12: Scaled CRL (ours) outperforms baselines...' Section 4.2 cites Figure 12 for the baseline comparison and Section 4.4 cites Figure 12 for the 256/1024-layer results. Duplicate numbering makes the references ambiguous and is a clear editorial error.

Section 4.2 claims 'over 50× gains in humanoid-based tasks,' and Figure 1's caption says gains range 'from doubling performance to 50× improvements on Humanoid-based tasks.' Table 1 reports Humanoid = 42×, Humanoid U-Maze = 40×, Humanoid Big Maze = 600×, and Ant Hardest Maze = 1.7×. Thus the '50×' and 'doubling' descriptions are inconsistent with the paper's own table.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3 vs Appendix Table 7 and Figure 9
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 3 defines the critic as a dot-product similarity f(s,a,g) = phi(s,a)^T psi(g). Appendix Table 7 lists the hyperparameter 'energy_function: L2,' and Figure 9 defines Q as the L2 distance ||phi(s,a) - psi(g)||_2. These are three different critic/energy definitions, and the paper never clarifies which one is actually used.

Figure 9 defines Q(s,a,g) = ||phi(s,a) - psi(g)||_2 and then describes 'high Q values' at the goal and high Q values near the start for the shallow network. With a positive L2 distance, states near the goal should have low distance and therefore low Q, not high Q. The sign/polarity of the visualized Q-function is inconsistent.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.4, 'Scaling the Actor vs. Critic Networks' and Figure 6
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text and Figure 6 caption say 'in Ant Big Maze, the actor matters more' / 'actor scaling to be more impactful.' The displayed Ant Big Maze values show critic scaling from depth 4 to 64 at actor depth 4 improves success from 61 to 462, whereas actor scaling from depth 4 to 64 at critic depth 4 improves success only from 61 to 72. Even at critic depth 64, actor scaling only changes 462 to 571. The displayed data therefore indicate critic scaling is much more impactful in Ant Big Maze.

predicted_errors.error_location: Reference 'Liu, H., Li, C., Wu, Q., and Lee, Y. J. (2024)'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The reference is 'Visual instruction tuning. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 36' with year 2024. The LLaVA paper 'Visual Instruction Tuning' appeared at NeurIPS 2023 (proceedings volume 36), so the year should be 2023 rather than 2024.
